intro.title: Search Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive search form component that allows users to input search terms and submit queries. You'll learn how to create reactive forms in Angular using the FormBuilder service to handle user input validation and form state management. The lesson covers essential Angular concepts including two-way data binding, form controls, and event handling to capture user interactions. You'll implement form validation to ensure proper user input and create a submit handler that processes the search query. By the end of this lesson, you'll have a fully functional search form that demonstrates how Angular's reactive forms system enables dynamic user interfaces with real-time feedback and validation.
intro.usecase: Search forms are fundamental components in countless web applications, from e-commerce sites like Amazon's product search to social media platforms like Twitter's tweet search functionality. Developers frequently implement search forms in admin dashboards for filtering user data, content management systems for finding articles or posts, and customer support portals for searching knowledge base articles. These forms typically include input validation, loading states, and result display logic that must be properly wired together using Angular's reactive forms and component communication patterns. Mastering search form implementation is essential for creating responsive, user-friendly interfaces that handle real-time filtering and data retrieval efficiently.
